E03 compares the learned allocator with the real label-free ThresholdAllocator at identical 750 verifier calls (25% budget). Learned minus threshold admitted rate has a paired bootstrap CI of [+0.412, +0.491], which favors the fixed rule. L3a, L3b and L3i confirm this with the same baseline. The baseline has no free labels, so the confound is controlled and W2 is false. Claim 3: every later entry reuses E01's pool (same model, task and proxy), so none can kill the claim. L3k shows an embedding AUC gain of 0.002 on that pool, and no neighbor ratio of 1.5 or more or AUC gain of 0.05 or more appears anywhere. The claim stays open and W3 is false.

E03 ran the real label-free ThresholdAllocator against LearnedAllocator at identical verifier calls (750 at 25%). Threshold catches 334 errors and learned catches 131. The paired CI for learned minus threshold admitted rate is [+0.412, +0.491], which favors the fixed rule. L3a and L3b repeat this with the same result. The threshold uses no free labels, so the free-label confound from E01 is controlled and W2 is false. Claim 3 is not killed. Every non-E01 entry uses E01's pool: same model, task and proxy. Only E01 reports the neighbor ratio, so no independent kill exists. No entry shows an embedding gain of 0.05 or more, so claim 3 is not supported either. W3 is false.
